requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects and secure_redirects) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_redirects=1, secure_redirects=1 for all/default (cmd-fd94bac4130a449f). A persistent config file /etc/sysctl.d/60-network-hardening.conf was created setting all/default accept_redirects=0 and secure_redirects=0 (cmd-7850c205dd16410b), applied via sysctl --system and per-interface sysctl -w including enp1s0 and lo (cmd-c41dc7c2ae714ce6, cmd-9870581801a24b9f), verified 0 across all/default/enp1s0 (cmd-d1f04fe61a624958). After a full reboot (boot_id changed from cce73776... to 485f521e..., cmd-d3e058606846491c), the values were re-verified as 0 for all/default/enp1s0 and the config file was still present (cmd-6bb76a1c113742c7), directly demonstrating persistence across restart.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed accept_source_route already 0 for all/default (cmd-fd94bac4130a449f). Explicit persistent directives were still added to the sysctl.d config file for all/default (cmd-7850c205dd16410b) and applied at runtime for all/default/enp1s0/lo (cmd-9870581801a24b9f), verified 0 across all/default/enp1s0 (cmd-d1f04fe61a624958). Post-reboot verification (boot_id changed, cmd-d3e058606846491c) confirmed accept_source_route remained 0 for all/default/enp1s0 and the config file persisted (cmd-6bb76a1c113742c7), directly demonstrating persistence across restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64 was captured along with baseline sysctl health (cmd-fd94bac4130a449f, cmd-31b3be3e8a0e4bed), matching the fixed before-prepare boot-identity snapshot. A reboot was triggered and acknowledged (cmd-f81f1fa01c574c12), connectivity was lost during the transition (cmd-661f62fe1b644dbe, cmd-a12a7ffe1c374b2f), and a different post-restart boot_id 485f521e-e3f6-41de-b9a9-d63b691f0f31 was observed (cmd-d3e058606846491c), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart recovery was confirmed via fresh uptime, restored sysctl hardening values, systemd-sysctl active, network interface up with IP, and systemctl is-system-running reporting 'running' (cmd-6bb76a1c113742c7, cmd-f45236e2d8c94c84), and the fixed after-executor snapshot shows no failed services and normal listening sockets.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes of the task — persistently disabling IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance (accept_redirects, secure_redirects) and source-routed packet acceptance (accept_source_route) on node1 — are satisfied with direct pre-change, applied-change, and post-reboot-verified evidence. The provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also fully and coherently demonstrated: pre-restart boot identity and health, restart acknowledgement, a changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered service/network/system state, consistent with the fixed before-prepare and after-executor snapshots. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were found.
limitations: accept_source_route was already 0 at baseline, so its persistent-disable behavior across reboot was confirmed via the new config file and runtime values rather than a redirects-style true baseline-to-disabled transition observed for that specific setting alone.

Per-interface enp1s0/lo accept_redirects and secure_redirects values are only set at runtime (sysctl -w) and not explicitly persisted per-interface in the config file (only all/default are persisted); persistence relies on the kernel's all/default AND-logic, which was directly confirmed effective for enp1s0 post-reboot (cmd-6bb76a1c113742c7), so this is not a functional gap but is noted as an implementation detail.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands in the timeline map clearly to task purposes: baseline capture (read-only), writing the persistent sysctl.d config (cmd-7850c205dd16410b), applying it via sysctl --system and per-interface sysctl -w (cmd-c41dc7c2ae714ce6, cmd-9870581801a24b9f), and the mandatory reboot (cmd-f81f1fa01c574c12). No unnecessary or unrelated mutations, troubleshooting experiments, or abandoned residue were found. The reboot left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the nohup-based reboot mechanism, which is a low-risk, expected byproduct of the sanctioned restart step rather than unwanted residue. No failed services or package-health regressions appear between before-prepare and after-executor snapshots.
